chunks: The two parents for whom Allah made gratitude obligatory are the two who gave birth to knowledge and inherited judgment, and the people were commanded to obey them. Then Allah said, “To Me is the destination”; so the destination of the servants is to Allah, and the proof of that is the two parents.
Then He turned the speech toward Ibn Hantamah and his companion, and He said concerning the specific and the general: “And if they strive with you that you associate with Me...”
He means regarding the وصية and turning away from the one whose obedience you were commanded to uphold: so do not obey the two of them, and do not listen to their words.
Then He turned the speech toward the two parents and said: “And keep company with the two of them in the world with kindness.”
He says: make the people know their merit and call to their path, and that is His saying: “And follow the path of the one who turns to Me; then to Me is your return.”
So he said: To Allah, then to us. Therefore have taqwa of Allah and do not disobey the two parents, for their pleasure is the pleasure of Allah, and their anger is the anger of Allah.

key_terms.رِضَاهُمَا: their pleasure, linked here to the pleasure of Allah
key_terms.سَخَطُ: anger or displeasure, attributed here to Allah through theirs
key_terms.ٱتَّبِعْ سَبِيلَ: follow the path, meaning adherence to their way
key_terms.ٱلْحُكْمَ: judgment or authority inherited by them
key_terms.ٱلْوَالِدَانِ: the two parents, interpreted here in a spiritual and authoritative sense
key_terms.ٱلْوَصِيَّةِ: the designation or testamentary appointment referred to in the passage

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith interpret the Quranic command to give thanks to one's parents and obey them?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a tafsir of the verses about gratitude to one's parents by interpreting the “two parents” in a higher spiritual sense linked to divinely mandated authority, knowledge, and judgment. It emphasizes obedience to those vested with rightful authority, dissociation from rival claimants, and recognition that their pleasure and displeasure are bound to Allah's pleasure and displeasure.
